label: Ning Li
narrative: Chinese-American physicist who emigrated in 1983 and spent two decades at the UAH Center for Space Plasma and Aeronomic Research working on gravitomagnetism, extending the Meissner effect from electromagnetism to gravity. She founded AC Gravity LLC in 1999, won a 448,970 dollar DoD grant in 2001, and moved into classified work at Redstone Arsenal after 2003. She was struck by a car on the UAH campus in 2014 and suffered permanent brain damage; reporting indicates the injury led to an Alzheimer’s diagnosis shortly afterward. She died of natural causes in 2021. The seven-year gap between the collision and her death substantially weakens any suspicious-death framing, and the case is retained both for the research continuity to Eskridge and because her research line is the subject of a FOIA-released DIA reference document, DIA-08-1003-013.
affiliations: UAH Center for Space Plasma and Aeronomic Research (1983-1999)
Redstone Arsenal / US Army AMCOM (classified, post-2003)
tierRationale: A conventional explanation is documented and holds: a 2014 campus vehicle collision, resulting brain damage, and death of natural causes seven years later. The DIA reference document on her research line shows institutional interest in the subject matter, not in her, and does not disturb that. Tier C stands and the seven-year gap remains the governing counterargument.

contested.text: His official service biography refutes the alleged early-2000s programmatic link. His early-2000s AFRL post, October 2001 to May 2004, was Materiel Wing Director of the SPACE VEHICLES Directorate and Commander of Phillips Research Site at Kirtland AFB, New Mexico. claims.text: The Mondaloy patent family is three US applications sharing a September 2001 priority: 09/954,835, 10/769,195 and 12/626,205, titled "Burn-resistant and high tensile strength metal alloys". Inventors are Monica A. Jacinto and Dallis Ann Hardwick, two of two. All three were ABANDONED and no US patent was ever granted. The trade name Mondaloy appears in none of them.

None of the three applications carries a government-interest clause. Established as absent rather than unfound: the full text of all three was searched for "government", "federally sponsor", "certain rights", "under contract" and "Air Force", zero matches on all five in all three, and the conventional heading is absent from the description. The patent record therefore names no funding agency and no contract number.

A patent on the alloy was GRANTED in the Russian Federation and never in the United States: RU2301276C2, filed 17 September 2002, granted 20 June 2007, assignee United Technologies Corporation, since lapsed. Recorded as a bare record fact. The ordinary explanation is prosecution and assignment mechanics at a company operating internationally.

She describes the Air Force relationship herself: "In 1999, we entered the first cost-sharing program with the Air Force Research Laboratory." The AFRL element named in Aerojet Rocketdyne's own 2016 release as co-developer of Mondaloy 200 is the Materials Directorate at Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio.

"Lead inventor" is not supported as stated. US patents designate no lead inventor and inventor order carries no legal weight. She is first-named of two; the other is Dallis Ann Hardwick of the Rockwell Science Center, who died in 2015. The alloy name is a portmanteau of both: Monica and Dallis.

label: Carl Grillmair

narrative: Shot once on his own front porch in Llano on February 16 2026. He has the strongest documented sequence in the entire file, and it is a sequence about the criminal justice system rather than about classified work. Someone reported his eventual killer for trespassing on December 20 2025; deputies found the man in Palmdale carrying a loaded unregistered rifle and arrested him on a felony weapons charge; he was released after three days; the charges were dismissed on February 5 or 6 2026; and he killed Grillmair eleven days later. Note the correction of August 7 2026: the chain has always been told as Grillmair reporting the man who killed him, and his widow told the BBC that her husband did not call 911. The sequence does not depend on who placed the call and holds without it. Grillmair studied dark matter and exoplanets and held no documented clearance, while working at Caltech IPAC, inside the institution that manages JPL. All three of those facts have to be visible at once, which is exactly why the three axes are not summed. His widow, Louise Grillmair, rejects the missing-scientists framing as absolute nonsense and says her husband would laugh at those promoting it; she believes he was targeted in a misguided revenge plot.

label: Neil McCasland
photo: Bernalillo County Sheriff's Office via NM DPS
narrative: Retired Major General and former AFRL commander, missing from Albuquerque since February 27 2026. The Bernalillo County Sheriff’s Office issued a formal correction set in June 2026 that dismantles most of what circulated about him: there is no Pentagon connection, likely a conflation with Riverside Research, a DoD contractor; he held a standard retiree clearance rather than active operational access; law enforcement emphasized his wife never said he made a desperate attempt to resign; and BCSO states there is no known connection between this case and the other missing-scientist cases. His wife wrote publicly that he had only very commonly held clearances since retiring more than thirteen years earlier, and that it seems quite unlikely he was taken to extract very dated secrets. Investigators confirmed he stepped down from consulting roles citing brain fog, though LA Magazine could not independently verify that in the FOIA documents it obtained. The search has stalled with no confirmed sighting since a store surveillance image on February 26 2026.

contested.text: His official service biography refutes the alleged early-2000s programmatic link. The AFRL cost-share began in 1999, when he was Chief Engineer of the Navstar GPS Joint Program Office at Los Angeles AFB and held no AFRL post at all. His early-2000s AFRL post, October 2001 to May 2004, was Materiel Wing Director of the SPACE VEHICLES Directorate and Commander of Phillips Research Site at Kirtland AFB, New Mexico. Mondaloy's documented government partner is the MATERIALS Directorate at Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio. Different directorate, different base, different technical domain. He did not command AFRL until May 2011, roughly a decade after the work in question, and commanding a laboratory is not overseeing a programme inside it. No document was found placing him and Reza on the same programme, contract, review board, panel, publication, award or facility at any time.

claims.text: Every one of the eight footnotes in the FBI letter is a press report: two Daily Mail, three New York Post, two The Hill. There is no government or primary source. The Committee describes its own basis as "unconfirmed public reporting" and writes "If the reports are accurate". It asked agencies about press coverage; it did not assert a pattern.

claims.text: On his access she writes: "It is true that when Neil was in the Air Force, he had access to some highly classified programs and information. He retired from the AF almost 13 years ago and has had only very commonly held clearances since. It seems quite unlikely that he was taken to extract very dated secrets from him." The last sentence is offered as her inference and reads as one. A spouse is not positioned to know the contents of a special access programme, so this bounds what was plausible rather than establishing it.

claims.text: On the UFO connection she writes that Neil "had a brief association with the UFO community through Tom DeLonge", worked with him "for a bit shortly after his Air Force retirement as an unpaid (Neil's choice) consultant on military and technical/scientific matters to lend verisimilitude to Tom's fiction book and media activities", and that after the Podesta emails were published there was less contact. She adds that "Neil does not have any special knowledge about the ET bodies and debris from the Roswell crash stored at Wright-Patt." She confirms the association and characterises it as minor; she does not deny it occurred, and she cites the Podesta hack herself.

contested.text: DeLonge's own account to Podesta describes a materially larger relationship: four months of work, a four-hour presentation on the entire project, and that McCasland "helped assemble my advisory team". The two accounts agree the association happened and disagree on its scope and significance. Neither is disinterested: she is his wife, and DeLonge was promoting a venture to a campaign chairman.

claims.text: An X account @TMBSPACESHIPS exists, display name "ELECTRIC PROPULSIVE SPACECRAFT SYSTEMS", joined November 2022. Its bio reads: "ELECTRIC PROPULSIVE SPACECRAFT and SPACECRAFT SYSTEMS MANUFACTURING. Experience: Retired 38 year Active Duty USAF PhD Engineer. AFIT/AETC/AFMC - UT/OU". That is a career shape consistent with an AFRL commander. It is a category, not an identification.

contested.text: The bio's two most specific identifiers do NOT match him. It reads "Retired 38 year Active Duty USAF PhD Engineer. AFIT/AETC/AFMC - UT/OU". McCasland was commissioned 30 May 1979 and retired July 2013, which is 34 years, not 38. And his degrees are USAFA 1979, MIT 1980 and MIT 1988: neither the University of Texas nor the University of Oklahoma appears anywhere in his education, and AFIT does not appear either. The parts of the bio that are generic to thousands of retired officers fit him; the two parts precise enough to identify a person do not.

claims.text: That the account is McCasland's is an attribution made by online sleuths across X and Reddit and relayed by press. NO official or law-enforcement source has confirmed it. The load-bearing detail, and the reason the claim is interesting at all, is that the account's final post is widely reported as 27 February 2026, the day he vanished. That date is NOT independently verified here and remains an outstanding ask. The Fear & Wine write-up's line that the account "is still active" is most likely saying it has not been deleted or suspended rather than that it is still posting, so it is probably not a contradiction of the last-post date. label: James Moffatt
photo: UAH Research and Engineering Support Center
narrative: Aerospace and defense engineer, retired Army aviation lieutenant colonel, founder of Moffatt Systems, and director of the Digital Engineering Transformation Lab at the UAH Research Center, with prior NASA work through Johnson Space Center. He died with three family members when his Mooney M20 came down near Union County Airport in South Carolina on April 17 2026. His son Andrew, a research engineer, was also killed. The FAA and NTSB are investigating and no cause has been determined. He is tagged media-linked rather than criteria-linked: he qualifies mainly because Fox News framed the story against the existing pattern, and he appears on no mainstream list, not Wikipedia, not the House Oversight list. Including him without that qualifier would be an instance of the near-enough effect the skeptical literature specifically names.
affiliations: UAH Research Center, Digital Engineering Transformation Lab
tierRationale: An aircraft accident under routine NTSB investigation with no determined cause and no family dispute. Qualifies on the media-linkage prong alone.
conflicts: Inclusion itself is contested. He appears on no mainstream list and was surfaced only by Fox and wire coverage plus advocacy trackers.
